quotes: LeakGuard runs under its own service account svc-leakguard-valves.
The account is not used by any staff member and has no interactive login.
findings.model_reasoning: These sentences show the agent uses a distinct service account. They also state it is not used by staff, which supports separation from staff login.

quotes: The account may close only the twelve isolation valves listed in annex B.
It cannot open valves or change pumps.
findings.model_reasoning: The quoted text limits the account to specific valve-closing actions and excludes other actions. It also says the permissions are reviewed quarterly.

quotes: Maria, operations lead, or the duty engineer approves each valve closure proposed by LeakGuard and can override or stop LeakGuard at any time.
findings.model_reasoning: This directly identifies named people who approve the agent's actions and can override or stop them.

quotes: After a closure, staff can reopen the valve manually from the console within 5 minutes; a field team can take over on site within 30 minutes.
findings.model_reasoning: This states the action can be reversed manually and gives a stated time for manual takeover.

quotes: Every LeakGuard action is written to the central log with time, account, action, target and result.
findings.model_reasoning: This sentence says every action is logged automatically and includes the required details: time, agent identity/account, action, target, and result.

quotes: Logs are kept for 12 months and reviewed weekly by the duty engineer.
findings.model_reasoning: This shows logs are retained for at least six months and are reviewed.

quotes: The plan covers malfunction or misuse of LeakGuard, including a wrongful valve closure.

findings.model_reasoning: The incident plan explicitly covers malfunction or misuse of the agent. It also includes the 24-hour, 72-hour, and one-month reporting deadlines.

quotes: The vendor shall notify Lakeside Water within 24 hours of any incident or vulnerability affecting LeakGuard.
findings.model_reasoning: This clause requires the vendor to notify the utility of incidents or vulnerabilities affecting the agent.
